free_tier.stated: N/A — DataLad is a wrapper over git-annex; quota is the special remote's. Its value here is that it makes 'dataset + N special remotes + reproducible publish' a supported, documented workflow instead of hand-written annex commands.

egress.terms: Inherited; DataLad's S3 walkthrough specifically configures `publicurl` so consumers clone the git metadata from GitHub and stream file content from the bucket with no credentials.

tooling: `datalad` CLI (Python), `datalad create-sibling-s3`, `datalad push --to <sibling>`, `datalad get`. Requires git-annex >= 10.20230802 for S3 publicurl on post-April-2023 buckets.
chaining: Combined with `datalad siblings` this is the cleanest way to shard one logical corpus across many free S3 accounts while keeping one coherent git history.
limits_note: Same as annex: no delete on LFS-backed remotes, per-store object caps. DataLad adds Python overhead and its own version-compat matrix (annex version pinned per feature).

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Used in production by academic consortia (OpenNeuro etc.) precisely for multi-TB datasets on donated storage — the most battle-tested 'big dataset on free/cheap stores' pattern that exists.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
